title: Continuation Identity and Admissibility
purpose: Define the identity continuation and establish the conditions under which continuation either succeeds or fails.

canonical_claims.statement: Identity is a continuation, not a static state.
Identity is the neutral element of continuation composition.
Admissibility governs the existence of continuation.
Failed continuation does not produce a continuation object.

formal_objects.name: Identity Continuation
formal_objects.definition: The lawful continuation that preserves condition A without changing its semantic state.

laws.name: Identity Law
laws.meaning: Every lawful condition possesses an identity continuation.

laws.name: Admissibility Gate
laws.meaning: Continuation cannot exist without satisfying admissibility.

laws.name: Composition Failure
laws.formal: If admissibility fails, composition is undefined.
laws.meaning: Failed continuation is not a valid continuation object.

validation_requirements: Identity continuation registered in the formal object registry.
Identity laws added to the textbook.
Composition examples verify left and right identity.
